messages:
maria: heads-up — found another mismatch between hosted/dedicated/private around ingress proxy responsibilities. current problem: each hosting mode implements auth, egress filtering, and tenant header enrichment in slightly different places which makes canary rollouts painful.
ash: can you sketch the painful path? example?
maria: sure — hosted does header enrichment in the edge lambda, dedicated does it in the runtime sidecar, private expects the customer sidecar to supply it. result: policy changes end up duplicated and we have 3 places to test.
jeff: ops concern: collapsing these layers into one delegated proxy sounds nice, but we need to be explicit about failure domains. If proxy is upstream and it fails, every mode degrades differently. what are SLO implications?
sara: +1 on clarity. tradeoffs: single delegated proxy (our code) vs small shim per mode. delegated proxy centralizes logic but increases blast radius; shims localize but duplicate code.
ash: proposal idea: "delegated ingress shim" pattern — minimal mode-specific shim that forwards to a shared proxy for policy, enrichment, and routing. shim responsibilities: TLS termination (mode-specific certs), tenant binding, network ACLs. shared proxy responsibilities: auth checks, quota decisions, enrichment templates, routing heuristics.
maria: that splits the failure domains neatly. shim handles networking and must enforce fallback to local defaults if shared proxy unreachable. fallback semantics must be explicit: reject vs best-effort enrich.
jeff: for private (air-gapped) customers, shared proxy will be optional — shim must be able to operate fully offline with a config snapshot. need clear manifest versioning.
sara: rollout plan suggestion: 1) add feature-flagged shared proxy in staging; 2) add shim adapter with config translation layer; 3) run shadow traffic for 2 weeks; 4) soft-cutover + telemetry gating.
ash: API surface idea for shim <-> proxy: small RPC like `CheckAuth(tenant, token) -> {allow, deny, reason}`, `Enrich(tenant, prefix) -> headers[]`, `Route(req_meta) -> model_variant`. Keep it language-agnostic, JSON-over-HTTP v1.
maria: include a tight version header and a compatibility matrix: sham/1.0 -> proxy/>=2.0 allowed, shim/2.0 requires proxy/3.x for new enrichment templates.
jeff: security note — for hosted we must ensure proxy never sees unredacted customer PII unless customer opted in. that implies an end-to-end masking policy and a shim-level redact hook.
sara: tests we need: a) shim failover simulations, b) manifest drift checks, c) latency tail tests for enrichment path (target 95p +5ms).
maria: implementation checklist: 1) define RPC spec + error codes, 2) shim adapter for private/dedicated/hosted, 3) proxy prototype (scala/golang?), 4) e2e shadow infra + tracing.
ash: one more nit — telemetry: instrument shim with latency and failure reason labels, and proxy with per-tenant decision traces. must be usable in Console for rollouts.
jeff: operational runbook: how to revert if proxy causes spikes: toggle shim to local-only mode, blackhole shared proxy endpoints via routing policy, publish incident note to oncall.
sara: iteration technique: start with enrichment-only in proxy (non-blocking), then move auth checks after confidence. reduces blast radius.
maria: agree. i'll draft an RFC with RPC spec and a simple sequence diagram. can we have a quick prototype spike next week?
ash: i can take the proxy spike, jeff can own shim adapters for dedicated/private, sara can own rollout gating & telemetry.
deploy-bot: CI pipeline started for branch `maria/ingress-shim-spike` — https://ci.internal/runs/9823 :eyes:
maria: thanks — meeting to align on Monday 10am PT. ping me if you want pre-read.
